title: STL thumbnail generation consumes excessive CPU and memory

status.label: Bound STL thumbnail resource use
status.detail: Reports correlate large meshes with extreme memory/CPU use. Current code limits output dimensions but loads the input mesh through StLReader.

next_action.label: Profile bounded synthetic STL cases
next_action.reason: Distinguish mesh expansion, repeated Explorer requests and retained resources before selecting limits.

judgment.rationale: Multiple reports and a concrete large-file workload support a maintainer-generated performance test. Input complexity is not bounded by the observed output-dimension check.
evidence: Original 0.75.1 report suspects a roughly 2 GB STL and describes 40% CPU on 32 threads with more than 16 GB RAM.
The author describes repeating memory-growth/CPU spikes; later commenters report relief after uninstalling or disabling STL thumbnails.
StlThumbnailProvider.GetThumbnail(Stream,uint) checks output dimensions, null and zero-length streams, then calls StLReader.Read(stream).
The reviewed timeline links duplicate #45343; no concrete fix PR was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Profile controlled mesh sizes and repeated thumbnail requests, then approve resource-budget enforcement appropriate for shell thumbnail generation.

fix_assessment.rationale: The repository-owned provider can reject or bound excessive thumbnail workloads; no existing concrete fix appeared in the reviewed linked work.

proposed_fixes.title: Apply input-complexity budgets before STL thumbnail mesh allocation
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: loading a large STL into StLReader and a full WPF mesh expands the file into much larger managed/rendering structures, while repeated shell thumbnail requests amplify allocation. Pulses alone do not prove a leak.
plan: Profile src/modules/previewpane/StlThumbnailProvider/StlThumbnailProvider.cs around StLReader.Read and rendering using increasing binary/ASCII mesh sizes and repeated calls.

Before full parsing, apply a documented conservative input/triangle budget suitable for thumbnails; safely validate binary headers and overflow, and use bounded handling for ASCII rather than trusting a declared count.

Return the existing no-thumbnail result for over-budget inputs; if profiling shows retained resources, deterministically release only the demonstrated stream/bitmap/rendering owners rather than treating every allocation spike as a leak.
Add UnitTests-StlThumbnailProvider coverage for normal meshes, over-budget inputs, malformed counts, nonseekable/error streams where supported and repeated generation.
verification: Representative small/medium STL thumbnails remain correct.
Over-budget STL inputs return promptly without full mesh allocation and without destabilizing Explorer.
Repeated accepted inputs have bounded retained memory; repeated rejected requests do not repeatedly parse the oversized file.

confidence.rationale: The inspected unbounded read and independent large-file reports support the resource-amplification hypothesis, but profiling must establish the dominant allocation and a suitable budget.

issue_context.summary: Large STL thumbnail workloads cause repeated severe CPU and memory spikes; disabling the provider alleviates the symptoms for affected users.
known_information: Original reporter identifies a roughly 2 GB model and quantifies resource usage.
Later comments independently report severe usage with many or massive STL files.
Current provider reads a full model before rendering a thumbnail; the visible maximum-size guard limits image dimensions, not model complexity.
Live issue is open and unassigned.
inferences: Full mesh expansion and repeated thumbnail requests may explain the usage; retained-memory leakage has not been established.
issue_context.analysis: A synthetic workload can test the suspected boundary without asking for a proprietary multi-gigabyte model. Start with bounded cases and treat safe refusal as an option for shell thumbnails.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the report, all three comments, timeline duplicate and related PR search.
Inspected upstream StlThumbnailProvider.GetThumbnail and located its sibling UnitTests-StlThumbnailProvider project.

actions.label: Profile STL input size and repeated requests

prerequisites: Use generated nonprivate STL assets and an isolated developer test session.
Set a conservative memory/time stop threshold; do not begin by loading a 2 GB model on a normal workstation.
steps: Generate valid binary and ASCII STL cases with increasing triangle counts and a small known-good control.
Measure single thumbnail calls with managed/native memory and CPU around parse versus render.
Repeat calls for the same file and then request thumbnails through Explorer to detect amplification.
Stop at the preset resource threshold, then test over-budget rejection in the candidate without fully loading the mesh.
Compare retained memory after requests complete to distinguish temporary expansion from a leak.
reproduce.expected_result: Normal thumbnails remain correct and oversized workloads are bounded or rejected before excessive allocations.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Generate a small reproducible corpus of valid binary and ASCII STL files with deterministic increasing triangle counts. Include malformed-count and empty controls. Default to modest sizes, print file sizes/counts, and require an explicit developer decision before creating very large assets; do not use proprietary CAD models.

actions.label: Approve STL thumbnail resource-budget plan
actions.note: Profile first and choose evidence-based limits; this lightweight plan does not claim a confirmed memory leak.
